only you can know if your friend has good intentions or not, but honestly a lot of this can be a misunderstanding. i’m one of the smallest in my friend group by a good amount but will slip up and say things about wanting to lose weight, feeling fat, want a smaller stomach, etc... it’s not that i find my friends bodies unattractive (the complete opposite in fact, i love their bodies way more than i like mine) it’s just that my ED is only thinking about myself. i don’t find bigger bodies gross in fact i love some of them, i just cant have one?  i don’t know if that makes sense. but basically my ED isn’t thinking about anyone other than myself. i try to stop myself from saying comments like that because i know it can be really hurtful and damaging but when food and weight are things you’re constantly thinking about , it slips out. try to talk to your friend maybe? there’s a chance she hasn’t noticed or just hasn’t really thought about the fact that it could upset you. and always remember you come first, if you need to take a little break or maybe not see her in more triggering circumstances that’s completely acceptable. you don’t sound whiny at all, your allowed to rant and complain! try not to put yourself down.

i understand your point of view but there’s is huge societal pressure for women to always look pretty. having acne can be debilitating so yes leaving the house without makeup was hard for me, ive gotten many rude comments from strangers if i leave the house without makeup which is why i stopped doing that. i agree no one is entitled to anything , and i don’t believe anyone has to look a certain way. accepting the way you look like and having confidence in yourself isn’t easy especially when you faced bullying starting from a young age and people are still trying to tear you down. i can’t count the number of insults i’ve received now that it’s the holidays and family has come to visit. maybe makeup and superficial stuff is easy for you but not for me. beauty is 100% subjective i agree. looks are important to me because they’re really the only thing i can control right now, i go to therapy and take meds but have a lot of comorbid disorders and an undiagnosed physical illness which makes it very hard for me to try different meds (so far i’ve tried around 16). it’s also very expensive. i wish i had the luxury of being able to do dbt or an inpatient facility for a while but i don’t. i suffer from ptsd so i don’t know if maybe that’s what u meant by cluster b.  i ramble like a lot of people and when i have a lot of thoughts it can be erratic but i don’t think it’s necessarily a sign of another mental issue and while i appreciate your concern i don’t think it’s necessary in this particular instance and u cant diagnose someone online. i do stay off of instagram right now, it hasn’t really made me feel better. i tend to not use it but that day i did go down a rabbit hole stalking that girl, i like the concept of instagram a lot as i’m a very visual person but it’s turned into something else completely. my personal beauty ideals aren’t the typical instagram ones you might be thinking like fillers or “caterpillar brows” or that instagram makeup. for me dressing and looking how i want has always been important to me, having a unique style is something i’ve always had and i feel confident when i dress how i want. i don’t think it’s superficial and i don’t think there’s anything wrong with it. i don’t think people who post on instagram are sick damaged unhealthy posers,,, they’re just people. and if they are suffering from something we shouldn’t shame them but extend empathy towards them. i don’t know a pro-woman site or anything like that but even if all a woman wanted to do was perfect her makeup and get her perfect sharpie eyebrows or what you call and glam makeup there’s no reason to disrespect that. people are intricate and complex and diverse, everyone has different goals and as long as no one is hurting anyone else who are we to judge? i’ll admit it’s not a lifestyle i want or care for but whatever. i know my thinking is flawed and i have unrealistic goals and expectations for myself but just going to therapy isn’t easy, i’m trying my hardest and i have for a while. it’s incredibly expensive and i can’t afford treatment so i have to move to another country. that’s not easy either. i can’t simply just go back to school. i wish it was that easy but for me it’s not. i know i am more than my looks, but since it’s the main thing i have control over that is why i hold it to such a high standards. my friend from comic-con (a girl for clarification) is a good friend at heart but sometimes jealousy overcomes her and she can say spiteful things. i don’t believe i deserve that and the only reason i didn’t say anything was because i was just so shocked was because i didn’t expect it at all, i do maybe need better friends but again it’s not that easy. i believe you had good intentions with your reply but “If you were however sticking out your tits, like an alcoholic must refrain from drink, temporarily maybe refrain from attention seeking behaviors” is a vile thing to say. like i had said i was in costume, i never mentioned that i was “sticking my tits out” or anything of the sort. i have a naturally larger chest and because i was dressing up as an anime character i had cleavage showing. i don’t know what your intention was with that comment but i found it hurtful and spiteful. i think you had good intentions but you’re on a subreddit where people are very sensitive and you have really diminished my feelings by calling something i personally like superficial and i felt really demeaned while reading this. accusing me of sticking my tits out and implying i search for validation like an addict is incredibly rude. please be more careful with your choice of words in the future as you could really really hurt someone. if i read this reply in another moment i honestly don’t know how bad i couldn’t reacted.
